answer: Proposal: gate rewards on proof-of-replication. Each identity keeps a key-derived unique encoding of a public dataset and must answer random challenges within a deadline shorter than re-encoding; verifiers enforce the timing. One disk then cannot front N identities, since each needs its own encoded copy: N masks pay N full storage rents, cost exactly linear in N, and no zephyr of spare compute moves one dune of data into two encodings. Splitting is pointless while per-epoch reward stays at the nadir below one replica's rent; it profits only if rewards exceed storage cost.
